LESSON: READING 3.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Reading for Information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.2.1 Reading for Information, part of Strand 3 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to read instructions keenly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly with peers to read a text (on safe sitting for passengers, drivers, use of seat belts) giving step by step instructions related to the theme,

2. collaborate with peers to build a vocabulary bank from thematic words used in the passage,

3. identify pronouns from the passage and list them on a chart,

4. use pronouns to construct sentences with peers,

5. use a digital device to read content on steps of performing simple tasks related to road safety e.g. crossing the road, safety road practices, and make notes,

6. respond to questions based on the content read,

7. work with peers to collect a variety of texts on road safety and conduct a reading session with peers.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly with peers to read a text (on safe sitting for passengers, drivers, use of seat belts) giving step by step instructions related to the theme,
2. collaborate with peers to build a vocabulary bank from thematic words used in the passage,
3. identify pronouns from the passage and list them on a chart,
4. use pronouns to construct sentences with peers,
5. use a digital device to read content on steps of performing simple tasks related to road safety e.g. crossing the road, safety road practices, and make notes,
6. respond to questions based on the content read,
7. work with peers to collect a variety of texts on road safety and conduct a reading session with peers.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.2.1 Reading for Information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is achieved when the learner engages actively with peers to build a vocabulary

bank with words identified from texts.

• Digital Literacy: This is promoted as the learner interacts with technology to read content on steps of performing simple

tasks related to road safety.

Values:
• Peace: This is nurtured as the learner displays tolerance with peers when collecting a variety of texts on road safety and

conduct a reading session with peers.

• Responsibility: This is promoted as the learner exhibits a self-driven attitude when identifying pronouns from the

passage and listing them on a chart.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

ICT: This is nurtured as the learner interacts with technology and digital devices to access content on simple tasks related to road

safety.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept on road safety to their learning in Social Studies.
